summary: Embedded dashboard panel pagination reset causes alert evaluation windows to be skipped
description:
Issue summary:
When an embedded dashboard with multiple paginated panels is viewed while a recent retention backfill job is running, pagination on embedded panels resets to page 1 intermittently. This reset shifts the time windows used by the client-side alert evaluation UI, resulting in alert evals that skip recent buckets (missing 1–3 minutes) and therefore suppress expected alerts.

Impact:
- Customer reports missed threshold alerts for a production route used in BeaconHealth AI’s triage workflow; they missed three alerts over a 45m window.
- Affected customers on enterprise tier using embedded widgets and long retention backfills.

Environment:
- Redwood Console (hosted) prod cluster serving eu-west and us-east; issue observed in us-east region.
- Browser repros on Chrome 112 and Safari 16.

Observed behavior:
- Opening an org-embedded dashboard with paginated panels during a retention backfill occasionally causes the panel to jump back to page 1.
- The client-side alert evaluation code uses visible panel page offsets to compute alert windows; after a reset, the evaluation skips the most recent N buckets causing missed alerts.

Expected behavior:
- Pagination state for embedded panels should be preserved (or decoupled from backend retention maintenance) and alert evaluation windows should remain continuous across retention backfill events.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer loads an embedded dashboard iframe that contains 3 paginated panels (each panel shows time-series with 1m buckets).
2) Trigger or schedule a retention backfill in us-east (we reproduced via backfill job id retention-backfill-20260310-1730).
3) Observe panel pagination behavior in the guest org session while the backfill runs (5–20m).
4) Check alert timeline: open alert eval history for the alert rule connected to the panel’s route metric and compare gaps to server ingest timeline.
logs: Console JS: Uncaught (at promise) Error: pagination-state-sync failed: 409 (conflict) — /api/console/embed/state (2026-03-10T17:42:03Z)
Browser network: GET /api/console/embed/state?org=beacon-health&pageToken=eyJ... returned 200 then 409 intermittently during backfill window

Server: retention-indexer: backfill job retention-backfill-20260310-1730 started at 2026-03-10T17:30:12Z, reindexed partition p-20260310-17-30; logs show short spikes of lock contention on embed_state table (see link)
comments: 2026-03-10 - Support (Maya Chen): Opened with BeaconHealth AI after they reported 3 missed alerts during a 45m window. Customer provided dashboard embed URL, alert rule id A-89321, and time of backfill. Asked for timeline and temporary mitigation steps.

2026-03-11 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Reproduced locally by running a retention backfill against a staging copy. Observed pagination state writes failing with 409s and client falling back to default page=1. Hypothesis: state writes are blocked by retention-indexer locks during partition repair which causes client fallback. Assigned to console team for fix + hotpatch.

2026-03-12 - Console Eng (Priya Nair): Confirmed pagination state write uses pessimistic row-level locking on embed_state; retention backfill sometimes reclusters the table leading to transient deadlocks. Proposed short-term mitigation: change client to honor last-known local pagination token when server returns 409. Long-term: make embed_state writes idempotent and use conditional upsert without locking.

2026-03-13 - Support (Maya Chen): Shared a screenshot and timestamp from BeaconHealth AI showing alert history gaps. Customer needs a workaround they can apply today; asked if an account-level toggle is possible to disable server-side pagination sync for embeds.

2026-03-14 - Diego Alvarez: Implemented and deployed a targeted client-side hotfix to staging that preserves local pagination token on 409 responses. Rolling to prod in a canary for us-east tonight. Filed linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-console/pull/7845.
investigation_notes: Checked DB traces for embed_state table during backfill: saw lock wait times up to 1400ms and repeated update retries from embed-sync workers.
Correlation: each 409 pagination reset lines up with a retention-indexer partition reindex event (retention-backfill-20260310-1730).
Repro steps successful on staging when artificially holding a table lock during pagination-state upsert. Client behavior falls back to page=1 when server signals conflict.
Related internal ticket INT-44321 flagged for making embed_state upserts idempotent and removal of row locks during reindexing.
resolution:
Temporary: client-side hotfix deployed to ensure local pagination token is preserved when server returns 409 conflict. Canary rolling in us-east (2026-03-14 22:00Z).
Permanent: engineering story created to change embed_state writes to conditional upsert and make retention-indexer reindex less disruptive (linked INT-44321). Also adding an org-level toggle to disable server-side pagination sync for embeds as a customer-facing mitigation.
Follow-up: postmortem and runbook update to include guidance for retention backfills impacting embed state (assigned to Priya Nair).
